graphEvents.label: Why do plain planning and research prompts return no recommendation
Default 0.8 threshold leaves planning candidates below the bar
Deep research bridge is routing-disabled with empty descriptors
Mutating commands stay at the explainer floor

label: The default confidence threshold is 0.8 with a 0.35 uncertainty ceiling; for the planning prompt the full candidate set is sk-doc 0.6202, sk-code 0.5923 and system-spec-kit 0.5887, so every candidate fails and the recommendation list is empty.

For the research prompt the candidates are system-spec-kit 0.5874, cli-external-orchestration 0.5759 and sk-prompt 0.5747; command-deep-research is projected with routingEnabled false and empty keywords, domains and intent signals, so it never enters the race.

A typed /speckit:plan prompt returns command-spec-kit and system-spec-kit at 0.82, but the bridge's entire keyword set is four slash markers, so it has no plain-language planning phrase a chat prompt could match.

The no-slash penalty is a rank-only minus 0.08 applied to command-kind candidates when the prompt contains no slash; it cannot create a recommendation from a failing candidate and only pushes commands below skills when both are close.

The mutating-command gate lifts a command off the read-only explainer floor only when skill.readOnly is true; the deriver sets that flag only for manifest routes whose mutating value is read-only, so add-only and mutating commands stay gated.

The gate's recall cost is measurable: show me the plan for the login page returns zero recommendations, while run the planning workflow for a new login feature returns sk-doc, cli-external-orchestration and sk-code at 0.82 instead of the planning command.

Fusion gives command intent only the explicit-author lane and generic lexical overlap; active non-doctor bridges carry either diagnostic doctor phrases or bare slash markers, so chat planning and research intent reaches a skill hub first.

direction: Lowering the confidence threshold alone as the fix
reason: At threshold 0 the planning prompt surfaces sk-doc, sk-code and system-spec-kit, not a command, so lower thresholds amplify wrong-skill routing

direction: Treating the no-slash penalty as the cause of zero recommendations
reason: The penalty only reorders already-passing candidates; the zero result comes from the 0.8 confidence floor and missing command descriptors
